vulnerability_analysis: The Milesinu contract has owner-only functions to set fee percentages (taxFee, DevFee, liquidityFee). By default, these are low (1%, 2%, 3%), but the owner can set them to arbitrarily high values. When fees are collected during token transfers, they accumulate in the contract as tokens. The swapAndLiquify function converts half of these tokens to ETH, sends half of that ETH to DevAddress, and uses the other half to add liquidity. By setting DevAddress to the attacker's address and enabling swapAndLiquify, the attacker can extract ETH from the contract.
attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the contract owner using vm.prank. 2. Set all three fees to high values (e.g., 30% each). 3. Set DevAddress to attacker's address. 4. Enable swapAndLiquify. 5. Perform token transfers to trigger fee collection. 6. Trigger swapAndLiquify manually by selling tokens to accumulate ETH in contract, then extracting via DevAddress share.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.prank to impersonate the owner. 2. Call setTaxFeePercent(30), setDevFeePercent(30), setLiquidityFeePercent(30). 3. Call setDevAddress(payable(attacker)). 4. Call setSwapAndLiquifyEnabled(true). 5. Transfer tokens between addresses to accumulate fees in contract. 6. Ensure contract has enough tokens to trigger swapAndLiquify (≥ numTokensSellToAddToLiquidity). 7. The next transfer from non-pair address will trigger swapAndLiquify, sending ETH to attacker via DevAddress.
